logic_node.action: Classify HF Stage A as at-risk for HF
logic_node.action_detail: Stage A (At Risk for HF): Patients at risk for HF but without symptoms, structural heart disease, or cardiac biomarker abnormalities. Therapeutic interventions aim to modify risk factors.

source_text: Therapeutic interventions in each stage aim to modify risk factors (stage A), treat risk and structural heart disease to prevent HF (stage B), and reduce symptoms, morbidity, and mortality (stages C and D).

logic_node.action: Classify HF Stage B as pre-HF
logic_node.action_detail: Stage B (Pre-HF): Patients without current or prior symptoms/signs of HF but with evidence of structural heart disease, abnormal cardiac function, or elevated natriuretic peptide levels. Therapeutic interventions aim to treat risk and structural heart disease to prevent HF.

source_text: Therapeutic interventions in each stage aim to modify risk factors (stage A), treat risk and structural heart disease to prevent HF (stage B), and reduce symptoms, morbidity, and mortality (stages C and D).

logic_node.action: Classify HF Stage C as symptomatic HF
logic_node.action_detail: Stage C (Symptomatic HF): Patients with current or prior symptoms and/or signs of HF caused by structural and/or functional cardiac abnormality. Therapeutic interventions aim to reduce symptoms, morbidity, and mortality.

source_text: Therapeutic interventions in each stage aim to modify risk factors (stage A), treat risk and structural heart disease to prevent HF (stage B), and reduce symptoms, morbidity, and mortality (stages C and D).

logic_node.action: Classify HF Stage D as advanced HF
logic_node.action_detail: Stage D (Advanced HF): Patients with severe symptoms and/or signs of HF at rest, recurrent hospitalizations despite guideline-directed management and therapy. Therapeutic interventions aim to reduce symptoms, morbidity, and mortality.

source_text: Therapeutic interventions in each stage aim to modify risk factors (stage A), treat risk and structural heart disease to prevent HF (stage B), and reduce symptoms, morbidity, and mortality (stages C and D).

logic_node.action: Use NYHA classification to characterize functional capacity
logic_node.action_detail: The NYHA classification (Classes I-IV) is used to characterize symptoms and functional capacity of patients with symptomatic HF (Stage C) or advanced HF (Stage D). NYHA class is an independent predictor of mortality and is used to determine eligibility for treatment strategies.

source_text: The NYHA classification is used to characterize symptoms and functional capacity of patients with symptomatic (stage C) HF or advanced HF (stage D). It is an independent predictor of mortality.

logic_node.action: Maintain Stage C classification despite becoming asymptomatic
logic_node.action_detail: A patient with symptomatic HF (Stage C) who becomes asymptomatic with treatment (NYHA Class I) should still be categorized as Stage C HF. HF staging does not regress even when symptoms resolve with therapy.

source_text: Although a patient with symptomatic HF (stage C) may become asymptomatic with treatment (NYHA class I), that patient will still be categorized as stage C HF.
